themes.blind: Is there a conversation waiting for your reply?
themes.caution: The more you hurry, the more you should confirm dates and content.
themes.diff: Which option makes necessary communication easier?
themes.letgo: Rather than thinking forever, a small reply is fine.
themes.want: If the conversation moves, what do you want to do first?

wa08.hint: The Eight of Wands has no person drawn — only wands flying in the same direction. It represents a flow where things advance all at once, beyond anyone's intentions. In a decision, timing — riding the flow — carries more value than time spent deliberating carefully. If there is a message you have been holding a reply to, or one you almost sent, now may be the time to send it. But the more momentum a period has, the easier oversights happen. Decide just three conditions to hold at minimum, then move, and you can feel safe.
wa08.scene: When a conversation suddenly starts coming together and you grow anxious about whether to proceed as-is, this card tells you the flow is on your side. Reversed, it is a season where messages easily cross or are delayed. Rather than chasing in impatience, prioritize organizing the routes of information into one.
wa08.check: Might the timing to ride the flow be exactly now? Can you name three conditions to confirm at minimum before moving? Is there a message you are holding back? Within the momentum, what is easy to overlook?

decision.text: In a situation where a sudden message or a reply is demanded, like being contacted, read this card by whether it is a timing to ride the flow, rather than by careful deliberation. But do not skip the one confirmation of reading the content before answering. Reversed, before pressing, organize the dates and content and check the gap of delays and miscommunication.

wa09.background: A person with a bandaged head holds a wand and looks around. Eight wands stand behind them. It holds both the experience of having worked hard, and the fear of being hurt again.
wa09.name: Nine of Wands

reversed.meaning: Are you refusing even help because you fear more trouble? Rather than forcing yourself onward, resting and finding people you can rely on matter too.

themes.blind: From a past failure, are you protecting yourself too much?
themes.caution: Do not push away the very people who would help you.
themes.diff: Which option spares you from striving too hard alone?
themes.letgo: You do not have to assume you will be hurt again.
themes.want: What kind of help would you be willing to accept?

wa09.story: A card about the strength of having continued this far, even with tiredness.
wa09.symbol: Fire / Wands (passion, action) / Number 9 (a trial before completion)

upright.meaning: Check what you have managed so far. If you want to continue, you can build in rest and help, and think of a way that does not strain you.

themes.blind: What made it possible for you to continue this far?
themes.caution: Rather than straining to the very end, decide how you will rest, too.
themes.diff: Which option lets you continue while taking rest?
themes.letgo: Admitting tiredness does not erase the effort so far.
themes.want: What do you want to see through to the end?

wa09.hint: The man in the Nine of Wands, bandage around his head, leans on his wand and still watches his surroundings. The goal is near, but past wounds make his judgment careful. In a decision, respect the wariness you learned from past failures, while calmly discerning whether it applies this time too. If a final push is what the situation needs, counting concretely what remains to be seen through before a line can be drawn makes the rest of the road visible.
wa09.scene: When you are torn about whether to quit or continue a long-kept challenge, this card indicates you may be at the point of 'just a little more.' Reversed, review whether your guard has become so hard that you refuse new help. When you are tired, taking rest before deciding is also a respectable choice.
wa09.check: Can you count what you need to see through before a line can be drawn? Does the wariness from past wounds apply this time too? Are you refusing people who would extend help? Might you be in a state that needs rest?

decision.text: In a situation of continuing a relationship you have been carefully maintaining, read this card by confirming what you have kept so far, and whether you can continue with rest and help built in. Reversed, check whether wariness that you might be hurt again is pushing away even help.

wa10.background: A person carries ten wands, walking bent forward. The wands block their view. It is the figure of someone whose tasks have piled up until there is no room left.
wa10.name: Ten of Wands

reversed.meaning: When you notice you cannot carry any more, think about how to reduce it. Deciding who to ask for what makes it easier to let go.

themes.blind: Is there work or a promise you could still let go of?
themes.caution: When you ask someone, share the content and the deadline too.
themes.diff: Which option is clearer about how to reduce the burden?
themes.letgo: You can ask for help before you reach your limit, not only after.
themes.want: If the load lightened, what would you spend time on?

wa10.story: A card about asking whether you are carrying too much work or too many roles.

upright.meaning: Are you trying to do everything yourself? Write out your tasks, and separate what you can ask others to do from what can wait.

themes.blind: Which of your tasks truly need to be yours?
themes.caution: Do not burn through your energy just from the wish to finish.
themes.diff: Which option lets you divide the roles and move forward?
themes.letgo: You do not have to accept everything you are asked to do.
themes.want: If you could put down one load, what would it be?

wa10.hint: The man in the Ten of Wands walks on, his view blocked by the bundle of wands he carries. The destination village is visible in the distance, yet the sheer amount of load slows his steps. In a decision, what is asked is not what new thing to take on, but what to put down. Write out the responsibilities you carry, and separate what must be yours from what can be handed to someone. Carrying everything alone is not necessarily sincerity. Sharing the load gets you to the destination faster and more surely.
wa10.scene: This card often appears when you cannot decline requests and are torn about a new one. Reversed, it is a sign that the resolve to finally put the load down is forming. Do not be ashamed to acknowledge your limit — decide concretely who you will hand what to, and the resolve moves into action.
wa10.check: Of the responsibilities you carry, which must be yours? Is there a load you could hand to someone? Before accepting something new, what should you put down? Is your inability to decline kindness, or anxiety?

decision.text: In a situation of letting go of over-carried work or roles, read this card by what you should put down so you can walk to your destination, rather than by whether to accept something new. Separate who you can ask from what can wait. Reversed, the moment you notice your limit is the time to reduce — deciding who to ask for what makes letting go easier.

wa11.background: A young person holds a wand and looks at the sprouts at its tip. The land around is wide and sandy. Experience is still small, but the feeling of finding something interesting is treasured.
wa11.name: Page of Wands

reversed.meaning: Do you start on impulse and soon jump to something else? First decide how far you will test this one thing.

themes.blind: Are you only adding new things?
themes.caution: Before quitting, check how far you actually tested it.
themes.diff: Which option grows your experience one thing at a time?
themes.letgo: You do not have to put a hand to everything.
themes.want: Which interest is honestly still alive?

wa11.story: A card about taking interest in something new and beginning to learn.
wa11.symbol: Fire / Wands (passion, action) / Court card: Page (news, learning)

upright.meaning: Look into what caught your attention, or try a little of it. Even if you are not good at first, trying is how you learn whether it fits you.

themes.blind: What has caught your interest, even slightly, lately?
themes.caution: Before trying, do not promise big results.
themes.diff: Which option lets you experience and learn lightly?
themes.letgo: You do not have to hold back just because you are a beginner.
themes.want: Learning about what makes you excited?

wa11.hint: The Page of Wands gazes at the young leaves sprouting at the tip of the wand. It is not yet in shape, but it represents news that moves the heart, and the sprout of interest. In a decision, it teaches that even if you cannot draw the finished form, the feeling of 'this interests me' may serve as material for judging. Add options for touching it on a trial basis — going to a briefing, trying an experience, hearing from someone who knows it well. Picking up small curiosities without ignoring them leads to the next big choice.
wa11.scene: This card stays close when you are interested in a new field but unsure whether you are serious. Reversed, watch the tendency for interest to drift and not last. Before starting, decide a small promise like 'I will try it at least three times,' and whims become easier to tell from true interest.
wa11.check: Is there a way to test the feeling of 'this interests me'? Is there a small chance to touch it — a briefing, a trial? Would that interest stay unfaded after three tries? Who could you ask to move one step forward?

decision.text: In a situation of trying a new learning or hobby, read this card by using the sprout of 'this interests me' as material even if you cannot picture the finished form, deciding first how far you will test it, and starting small. Reversed, narrow to one thing first, so you do not start on impulse and quickly turn fickle.

wa12.background: A knight holding a wand is about to ride out on horseback. The pattern on their clothes suggests flames. It shows the power to act, and the feeling of heading somewhere new.
wa12.name: Knight of Wands

reversed.meaning: Is your wish to move fast so strong that you skip checking and asking? Confirm your own schedule and the people around you before you move.

themes.blind: Has moving fast itself become the goal?
themes.caution: Check the time and cost after you start, too.
themes.diff: Which option makes it easier to match the pace of those around you?
themes.letgo: You do not have to call a slow result a failure.
themes.want: If you did not have to hurry, what would you value?

wa12.story: A card about moving with momentum toward what you want to do.
wa12.symbol: Fire / Wands (passion, action) / Court card: Knight (action, drive)

upright.meaning: Turn the feeling of wanting to try into an actual step. While using your momentum, you can also watch that you do not overspend time or money.

themes.blind: Is there a small action that could use your momentum?
themes.caution: Check other people's circumstances and your own schedule, too.
themes.diff: Which option turns motivation into real action more easily?
themes.letgo: You do not have to wait until preparation is perfect.
themes.want: What would you like to challenge yourself with now?

wa12.hint: The Knight of Wands wears a cloak patterned with flames and gallops across the desert on a rearing horse. It is a card symbolizing the power to leap straight toward a goal. In a decision, it becomes a detonator for when you cannot move from overthinking. Decide just one most important goal for this choice, and resolve to arrange the other details as you run. But a charge on momentum alone runs out of breath. Drawing just the first week's itinerary concretely in advance is the wise move.
wa12.scene: When you are torn about stepping into a bold challenge, this card stands on the side of action. Reversed, take a breath and check whether short temper or impatience is rushing your judgment. Before advancing, on the momentum of deciding, into procedures that are hard to undo — contracts, resignations — even a single night's pause changes how things look.
wa12.check: Can you name the single most important goal in this choice? Is the itinerary of the first week drawn concretely? Are you about to advance, on momentum, into a procedure that cannot be undone? Would your feelings change after a night's sleep?

decision.text: In a situation where overthinking keeps you from moving, like independence, read this card as a detonator that turns momentum into a step. But keep a brake on overspending time and money, and on skipping consultation. Reversed, insert just one check — the schedules around you and the necessary confirmations — before charging ahead.

wa13.background: The queen holds a wand and a sunflower, with a black cat at her feet. Her confident seat shows trust in herself, and a posture that welcomes people warmly.
wa13.name: Queen of Wands

reversed.meaning: Are you making yourself small by comparing with those around you? Turn your eyes to what you can enjoy for yourself, not to earn praise.

themes.blind: Looking only at others' good points, are you making yourself small?
themes.caution: Do not turn anxiety into harsh words toward others.
themes.diff: Which option lets you keep your own pace without comparing too much?
themes.letgo: You do not have to feel you must stand out more than anyone.
themes.want: What would you like to enjoy just for yourself?

wa13.story: A card about treasuring who you are and sharing energy with those around you.
wa13.symbol: Fire / Wands (passion, action) / Court card: Queen (charm, confidence)

upright.meaning: Instead of only imitating others, try your own favorite way too. Acknowledging your strengths makes it easier to notice others' strengths as well.

themes.blind: Have you forgotten your own favorite way of doing things?
themes.caution: Even with confidence, treasure others' differences too.
themes.diff: Which option lets you be with people as yourself?
themes.letgo: Acknowledging your good points is not the same as boasting.
themes.want: If you stopped comparing, what do you like about yourself?

wa13.hint: The Queen of Wands sits on her throne holding a sunflower, with a black cat at her feet. She holds both bright charm and a sharp intuition kept within. In a decision, use as your standard whether you can be natural, and whether you can bring out your power to draw people in. More than a choice matched to the expectations around you, the path where your true self lives lasts longer. As the black cat suggests, listening to unease that is hard to put into words also matters.
wa13.scene: This is a reassuring card when you are torn about a role in front of people, or starting something under your own name. Reversed, check whether feelings of comparison or jealousy are distorting your choice. Return to the viewpoint of choosing a place where you can shine, rather than to beat someone, and the indecision loosens.
wa13.check: Having made that choice, can you see yourself smiling naturally? Which way lets your true self live, rather than the expectations around you? Are you overlooking an unease that is hard to put into words? Is a feeling of comparing yourself with someone mixed in?

decision.text: When torn, in a situation involving people, between matching those around you and showing who you are, read this card by the standard of whether you can be natural. The more you acknowledge your own good points, the more you can see others' too. Reversed, turn your eyes to what you can enjoy rather than be praised for, so you do not make yourself small by comparing.

wa14.background: The king sits holding a wand with sprouts. Lions and similar motifs appear on the chair and clothes. It shows the power to tell people what you envision and turn it into action.
wa14.name: King of Wands
wa14.story: A card about sharing a goal and moving forward together with companions.
wa14.symbol: Fire / Wands (passion, action) / Court card: King (leadership, vision)

upright.meaning: Share not only what you want to do, but why. Listening to the opinions and strengths of the people around you makes it easier to move together.

themes.blind: Has the reason behind the goal reached your companions too?
themes.caution: Before moving people, listen to their opinions and circumstances.
themes.diff: Which option makes cooperation toward the same goal easier?
themes.letgo: You do not have to advance everything alone.
themes.want: With whom, and what, do you want to make real?

reversed.meaning: Are you rushing people along, assuming you are the only one who understands? Check the goal and the approach in words that reach the other person too.

themes.blind: Has the plan become one only you are satisfied with?
themes.caution: Before rushing others, check whether your explanation is enough.
themes.want: Do you want people to follow you, or to move forward together?
themes.letgo: It is fine to change your own plan.
themes.diff: Which option makes it easier for everyone to speak up?

wa14.hint: The King of Wands holds a sprouting wand and sits on his throne, gazing into the distance. He is a leader who decides things from a large vision, not from immediate gain and loss. In a decision, draw first the picture of how you want to be in three years, and judge by whether the choice brings you closer to it. Because you have the power to draw others in, being conscious that your decisions affect others matters too. Once you show the direction, the breadth to leave the details to people you trust is also asked of you.
wa14.scene: When you stand in the position of deciding a large policy on behalf of a team or family, this card says you may raise your flag without hesitation. Reversed, inspect whether you are charging ahead by sole decision and missing the voices around you. Listening carefully to even one opposing opinion raises the quality of the decision remarkably.
wa14.check: Can you draw, as a single picture, how you want to be in three years? Which choice brings you closer to that picture? Have you thought about how your decision affects the people around you? Are you ready to entrust the parts that can be entrusted?

decision.text: In a situation of bringing people together, like independence or starting a business, read this card as deciding from the outlook of how you want to be in three years, rather than immediate gain and loss. Sharing even your 'why' makes it easier for those around you to advance. Reversed, check in words that reach the other person whether you are imposing your thinking and rushing people along.

cu01.background: A hand from a cloud holds a cup, and water overflows from it. Flowers bloom on the water's surface and a white bird flies above — receiving the feelings born in your heart.
cu01.name: Ace of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you holding your feelings in, or matching others too much? First, quietly check how you yourself are feeling.

themes.blind: Matching others, are you bottling up your feelings?
themes.caution: When you are tired, you do not have to force yourself to have fun.
themes.diff: Which option lets you express your feelings without strain?
themes.letgo: You do not always have to please the other person.
themes.want: What do you really want to tell, and to whom?

cu01.story: A card about the beginning of caring for someone, and of a heart being moved.

upright.meaning: Turn your eyes to feelings like joy, affection, and gratitude. You can also try telling the other person, in a way that does not strain you.

themes.blind: Have you noticed what made you happy lately?
themes.caution: Even when feelings run high, do not make promises you cannot keep.
themes.diff: Which option lets you treasure your own feelings?
themes.letgo: You do not have to hold back from accepting kindness.
themes.want: What person or thing do you honestly hold dear?

cu01.hint: The Ace of Cups is a scene of water overflowing from a cup offered from the clouds. It represents a feeling of the heart being fulfilled ahead of logic, and the beginning of caring for something. In a decision, rather than the score on a table of conditions, check whether imagining yourself having chosen it warms your heart. The overflowing water circulates by being shared, not only received. Whether that choice enriches not only you, but your relationships with the people close to you, is also important material for judgment.
cu01.scene: When choosing relationships or a new place to belong, your head may be torn while your heart already knows the answer. This card says you may trust that voice. Reversed, your heart may be closed, in a state where nothing you choose would fulfill you. Before deciding, first secure time to care for yourself.
cu01.check: When you imagine that choice, does your heart grow warm, or heavy? Can you share the joy you received with someone? Is the heart's voice being drowned out by the score on a table of conditions? Is the person you are now ready to be fulfilled?

decision.text: In a situation where feelings are newly born, like a confession, read this card by the movement of the heart itself — 'I like them' — rather than by a score of conditions. You can choose a step that shares it in a way that does not strain you. Reversed, first quietly check your own senses, so that hiding your feelings does not leave yourself behind.

cu02.background: Two people face each other, each offering their cup. A winged lion appears above them — a scene of meeting another person at the same eye level.
cu02.name: Two of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you skipping the conversation because you assume they understand? Check how each of you is actually feeling now.

themes.blind: Even with the same intention, might you be receiving things differently?
themes.caution: Before blaming based on assumptions, listen.
themes.diff: Which option lets you talk things out even when you differ?
themes.letgo: It is fine for your feelings not to match in everything.
themes.want: What do you want the other person to understand about you?

cu02.story: A card about caring for each other and exchanging feelings.

upright.meaning: After sharing your feelings, listen to the other person's. It is a hint for thinking about a relationship where neither side alone endures.

themes.blind: Are you making time to hear the other person?
themes.caution: Make sure neither side alone is enduring.
themes.diff: Which option lets you confirm each other's feelings?
themes.letgo: You do not have to decide the answer alone.
themes.want: What would you like to share with the other person?

cu02.hint: The Two of Cups is a scene of two people facing each other and exchanging cups. It represents a relationship of mutual respect as equals, where neither stands above the other. In a decision, the key is searching for a form that both the other person and you can accept, rather than your own gain and loss alone. If you are torn about a partnership, joint work, or choosing a partner, check whether you can be natural when listening to them. The ease of exchanging words is the best foundation of a long relationship.
cu02.scene: When you are torn about teaming up with someone, or advancing a relationship a step, this card shows you may proceed on the premise of trust. Reversed, inspect whether the balance of feelings and burdens has collapsed. Sharing just one hard-to-say thing can clarify where the relationship is heading.
cu02.check: Are you and the other person facing each other as equals? Can you be natural in front of them? Have you searched for a form you can both accept? Is it a relationship where you can share even one hard-to-say thing? Is the balance of burdens in place?

decision.text: In a situation two people decide together, like marriage, read this card by whether the form is one both can accept without either enduring, rather than by your own gain and loss alone. After sharing your feelings, hearing the other person's feelings is part of the material. Reversed, check whether you are skipping the conversation on the assumption that they must understand.

cu03.background: Three people stand in a circle, raising their cups high. Fruit lies at their feet — enjoying time together and celebrating what was accomplished.
cu03.name: Three of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you tiring yourself out or straining by going along with the mood? Treasure both the time together and the time you rest alone.

themes.blind: Are you tiring yourself by matching the mood of the room?
themes.caution: Even if you hear gossip, do not spread it without checking.
themes.diff: Which option lets you be with people at your own pace?
themes.letgo: You do not have to answer every invitation.
themes.want: Might you actually want some time alone, too?

cu03.story: A card about sharing joy with companions and supporting each other.

upright.meaning: Share your good news, or talk with a friend you trust. You may find an idea you would never have thought of alone.

themes.blind: Is there someone who would celebrate with you?
themes.caution: Even in fun company, avoid company that strains you.
themes.diff: Which option comes with companions who support each other?
themes.letgo: You do not have to keep striving alone.
themes.want: With what kind of people can you laugh with relief?

cu03.hint: In the Three of Cups, three women raise their cups high to celebrate the harvest. It is a situation where sharing joy with companions holds more value than achieving alone. In a decision, think about who that choice will have you spend time with. Even under the same conditions, an environment with companions you click with often lets you show more of your strength. When torn, talking to a trusted friend can let your true feelings surface inside the conversation.
cu03.scene: This card often appears when you are torn about joining a community, or starting something together with companions. Reversed, check whether fun is sweeping you into postponing important things, or whether gossip is swaying you. Even inside the circle, do not let go of your own axis of judgment.
cu03.check: With that choice, who will you spend time with? Are the companions you want to share joy with there? Swept by fun, are you postponing something important? Inside the circle, can you keep your own axis of judgment?

decision.text: In a situation of sharing joy, like drinks with friends, read this card as talking to a trusted companion before deciding all alone. An idea you would never have thought of alone may appear. Reversed, value time to rest alone too, so the mood of the room does not tire you out.

cu04.background: Before a person sitting with crossed arms under a tree stand three cups. A hand from a cloud offers one more, but the person is not looking — not noticing what is already there, or a new invitation.
cu04.name: Four of Cups

reversed.meaning: Turn your eyes to something you never cared about before. From an easy invitation or a small pleasure, you can test whether your feelings move.

themes.blind: Have you noticed a good point you could not see before?
themes.caution: Even if interest returns, do not add too many plans.
themes.diff: Which option makes it easier to test the interest that returned?
themes.letgo: It is fine to reconsider something you once declined.
themes.want: What would you like to try, on a small scale?

cu04.story: A card about times when your heart is not in it and the good in front of you is hard to notice.

upright.meaning: If nothing feels interesting, check whether you are tired. After resting, you can look at the options you have once more.

themes.blind: Might you be unable to feel interest because you are tired?
themes.caution: Do not refuse everything based only on the mood of the moment.
themes.diff: Which option lets you rest, then think again?
themes.letgo: You do not have to love something right away.
themes.want: What might move your feelings, even a little?

cu04.hint: The young person in the Four of Cups sits with crossed arms, noticing neither the cups before them nor the new cup offered from the clouds. It is not that they are unfulfilled — boredom and weariness have dulled their senses. In a decision, when you feel 'nothing appeals to me,' suspect whether the cause lies not in the options but in your own condition. Changing your environment a little, resting, or talking with someone can restore your sensitivity, and an overlooked opportunity may suddenly shine.
cu04.scene: When you are torn about declining an invitation or proposal, this card asks: 'do you truly have no interest, or are you just tired?' Reversed, there is a sign of escaping stagnation. Looking once more at an offer you once declined may reveal a form you can accept now.
cu04.check: Is feeling that nothing appeals to you the fault of the options, or of your own tiredness? Are you overlooking an opportunity being offered right in front of you? If you rested or changed your environment, might things look different?

decision.text: In a situation where every option looks faded, like being unable to feel like starting a side job, read this card first by whether your senses are dulled by tiredness or weariness, rather than by a problem with your power to choose. Reversed, check whether there is a sign that your feelings are beginning to move toward an invitation you used to pass by, or a small pleasure.

cu05.background: A person in black clothing looks at three fallen cups. Two more still stand behind them. It holds both permission to grieve, and the possibility that support remains.
cu05.name: Five of Cups

reversed.meaning: Check not only what was lost, but the support that remains. Even while sadness continues, you can lean on people little by little.

themes.blind: Are you overlooking the ways things have become a little easier?
themes.caution: Do not hide your feelings to appear fine.
themes.diff: Which option lets you move forward using the support you have?
themes.letgo: You do not have to give up on what comes next because of what happened before.
themes.want: From here on, with what kind of people do you want to spend time?

cu05.story: A card about grief for what was lost, and seeing what still remains.

upright.meaning: You do not have to force hard feelings away. When you settle, turn your eyes also to the people and things still beside you.

themes.blind: What support is still beside you now?
themes.caution: In your sadness, you do not have to rush a big decision.
themes.diff: Which option lets you accept support while acknowledging what was lost?
themes.letgo: You do not have to blame yourself for being sad.
themes.want: What do you want to treasure now?

cu05.hint: The figure in the Five of Cups gazes down at three spilled cups. But behind them, two cups still stand. In a decision, check whether the size of what you lost is stealing your eyes from the options that remain. There is no need to forcibly erase sadness or regret. But once your feelings settle, looking back and writing down what is still in your hands makes the road ahead appear like a bridge.
cu05.scene: This card stays close after a failure or a parting, when you are torn about challenging yourself once more. Reversed, there is a sign of recovery, a stage where you can turn your eyes to what remains. Do not rush a big decision — start by regaining small daily routines, and the power to judge returns too.
cu05.check: Can you write down not what you lost, but what still remains in your hands? Are you taking enough time to feel your sadness? What are the two cups still standing, for you now? When might you be ready to cross the bridge?

decision.text: In a situation of facing something you might lose, like lending money, read this card by lining up not only the size of what was lost, but what support and relationships remain. Reversed, even if your feelings are sunken, start rebuilding from the parts where you can rely on people.

cu06.background: A child hands a cup of flowers to another child. Old houses and cups of flowers are around them. It shows the feeling of giving a gift, and memories that feel safe.
cu06.name: Six of Cups

reversed.meaning: Thinking the past was better, are you overlooking what you have now? While treasuring the memories, think of a way of choosing that fits who you are today.

themes.blind: Are you remembering only the good parts of the past?
themes.caution: Check whether the old way still fits now.
themes.diff: Which option fits your current life and hopes?
themes.letgo: Your way of choosing does not have to match your past self.
themes.want: Do you want to return to the past, or do you want to feel safe?

cu06.story: A card about fond memories and honest kindness.

upright.meaning: Recall what you enjoyed before, and the people who helped you. From there, you may find what you still want to treasure now.

themes.blind: Is there a past experience that helped you?
themes.caution: Check what is different between then and now, too.
themes.diff: Which option lets you bring a treasured memory into the present?
themes.letgo: It is fine to show honest kindness.
themes.want: What has stayed precious to you, unchanged from before?

cu06.hint: The Six of Cups is a scene full of nostalgia: a child offering a cup filled with flowers. It represents pure goodwill without calculation, and a return to one's origin. In a decision, recall what you loved as a child, and the values your past self treasured. The answer to your indecision may, unexpectedly, sleep in the past. A reunion with an old acquaintance may also bring a new opportunity. But choosing on nostalgia alone can leave you with something that no longer fits who you are now.
cu06.scene: This card often appears when you are torn about returning to a former workplace or hometown, or teaming up with an old friend. Reversed, inspect whether attachment to the past is binding your judgment now. Asking not 'those days were good,' but 'what from those days can I apply now?' turns it into a forward-looking choice.
cu06.check: If you were your childhood self, which would you choose? Can you apply the values you treasured long ago to this choice? Are you about to choose on nostalgia alone? What from the past will you bring out, and what will you leave behind?

decision.text: In a situation where feelings for the other person come first, like choosing a present, read this card by what once delighted them and by your shared memories, rather than by price or market rate. Reversed, check whether leaning too much on 'the past was better' makes you overlook the other person's tastes as they are now.

cu07.background: Seven cups float on clouds, holding jewels, a castle, creatures, and more. A person looks up from below. Pleasant imagination spreads, and the real picture becomes hard to see.
cu07.name: Seven of Cups
cu07.story: A card about having so many attractive candidates that choosing becomes difficult.

upright.meaning: Are you comparing only by the impression that something looks fun? Looking into the time and effort actually required makes choosing easier.

themes.blind: Are you comparing only by how fun things look?
themes.caution: Check the time and cost required, too.
themes.diff: Which option makes it easier to verify whether you can actually try it?
themes.letgo: You do not have to choose everything at once.
themes.want: What do you want even if no one praises you for it?

reversed.meaning: Separate imagination from what you can actually do. Rather than choosing everything, this is a hint to decide on one thing you can try now.

themes.blind: Has a reason to narrow the candidates come into view?
themes.caution: Do not erase what you like just because something is realistic.
themes.want: Which one does the person you are now truly want to take on?
themes.letgo: It is fine to change a plan you once imagined.
themes.diff: Which option is where what you can do and what you wish for overlap?

cu07.hint: In the Seven of Cups, various treasures and monsters float inside seven cups above the clouds. It is a state where the sheer number of options steals your eyes, and which is real becomes hard to tell. In a decision, start by cutting dreams apart from plans. For each option, keep only those where you can write 'next week, I will concretely do this' — and the candidates above the clouds narrow on their own. The more attractive something looks, the more you need the calm to check for hidden conditions behind it.
cu07.scene: When you have too many things you want to do and cannot decide, this card reflects exactly that state. Reversed, the power to narrow down realistically is returning. Accept the pain of not being able to choose everything, decide on just one for this season, and the remaining dreams will not disappear — they will wait their turn.
cu07.check: For each option, can you write what you would concretely do next week? Behind the attractive-looking ones, are there hidden conditions? Can you distinguish dreams from plans? If you chose just one for this season, which would it be?

decision.text: In a situation where candidates have multiplied too much, like a big purchase, read this card by separating the impression that something looks fun from the time and effort it actually requires. Cutting dreams apart from plans reveals the real candidates. Reversed, stop trying to choose everything, and narrow to the one you can try now.

cu08.background: A person leaves eight cups behind and walks toward the mountains with a staff. The moon is in the sky — feeling that something is missing, and searching for another path.
cu08.name: Eight of Cups

reversed.meaning: You may want to change, yet stay in the same place out of anxiety. Write down, separately, your reasons to stay and your reasons to leave.

themes.blind: Can you separate your reasons to stay from your fear of moving?
themes.caution: Do not endure for a long time while unable to decide.
themes.diff: Which option lets you decide on a small ending or a small preparation?
themes.letgo: You do not have to continue just because you have continued for a long time.
themes.want: If no one stopped you, what would you want to do?

cu08.story: A card about drawing a line under where you are and searching for something that matters more.

upright.meaning: Consider whether what you are continuing still fits who you are now. Once you check your reason for wanting to leave, you can decide the preparation you need next.

themes.blind: Why does continuing leave you unfulfilled?
themes.caution: Think about the plan after you leave, and the people you can rely on.
themes.diff: Which option connects to what you hope for next?
themes.letgo: It is fine to review something you once chose.
themes.want: What do you want to value more than you do now?

cu08.hint: The figure in the Eight of Cups leaves neatly stacked cups behind and walks out into the moonlit mountains. Not because they failed, but in search of something unfulfilled, they leave of their own accord. In a decision, even in circumstances that look blessed from outside, it teaches that if your heart has left, you may advance to what is next. But before leaving, check whether you can say in one phrase what you are seeking. Leaving with a vague purpose tends to carry the same emptiness into the next place.
cu08.scene: When you are torn about letting go of a stable job or relationship, this card shows that the season of 'graduation' has come. Reversed, discern whether you are staying out of inertia, or whether there is still something to learn. Returning is not necessarily retreating — it can be a choice to clear up what was left undone.
cu08.check: Can you state your reason for wanting to leave in a single phrase? Is what you seek truly in the next place? Are you resolved to set down what you have built up? Is there still something left to learn here?

decision.text: In a situation of leaving circumstances that look blessed from the outside, like resigning, read this card by putting into words not that you failed, but what you are unfulfilled by. Reversed, write your reasons to stay and your reasons to leave separately, and check the true shape of why you cannot move.

cu09.background: A person sits contentedly with nine cups lined up behind them. It is a scene where the things they find delightful are gathered. It is also a hint for thinking about what makes you happy.
cu09.name: Nine of Cups

reversed.meaning: Even with the thing you wanted, your heart may stay unfulfilled. Think again about what you truly wanted.

themes.blind: Do you keep seeking without deciding what would satisfy you?
themes.caution: Do not try to fill a gap in your heart with money or things alone.
themes.diff: Which option settles not only the surface, but your feelings too?
themes.letgo: You do not have to want what others envy.
themes.want: Do you truly want the thing itself, or peace of mind and connection?

cu09.story: A card about confirming your own wishes and what satisfies you.
cu09.symbol: Water / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Number 9 (satisfaction, wishes fulfilled)

upright.meaning: Take your time to savor the good things you already have. It is a hint to choose what satisfies you, rather than what others wish for.

themes.blind: What are you already fulfilled by?
themes.caution: Even when happy, do not grow greedy and add too much.
themes.diff: Which option leads to your own satisfaction rather than others' evaluation?
themes.letgo: It is fine to enjoy what you have gained.
themes.want: What kind of state is happiness, for you?

cu09.hint: The man in the Nine of Cups sits contentedly with crossed arms, the lined-up cups at his back. It is a card representing a state where a wish has come true and both heart and life are fulfilled. In a decision, try defining in advance what would let you say 'I am satisfied.' Once the standard is clear, the option that meets it is surprisingly easy to find. Noticing the parts where you are already fulfilled may also surface the option of not forcing yourself to aim higher.
cu09.scene: This card often appears after you achieve a goal, when you are torn between aiming higher still and enjoying where you are. Reversed, check whether you feel emptiness despite supposedly being fulfilled. Rather than increasing the amount, thinking about who to share it with changes the quality of satisfaction.
cu09.check: Can you define, in advance, what 'satisfaction' means for you? Have you noticed the parts where you are already fulfilled? Is your reason for aiming higher from your true heart? Who do you want to share the joy with?

decision.text: In a situation of deciding the form of a wedding, read this card by the standard of what the two of you can be satisfied with, rather than the impressiveness others wish for. Leave room to savor the good things you already have, too. Reversed, think again about what you truly wanted, and why having what you supposedly wanted does not fulfill your heart.

cu10.background: Ten cups line up inside a rainbow. Below, adults and children rejoice, with a house nearby — being with people who matter, at ease.
cu10.name: Ten of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you hiding your true feelings to look close? Even if you are not all the same, you can look for a way for everyone to feel at ease.

themes.blind: Are you straining to appear close?
themes.caution: Do not blame by comparing with an ideal family or group.
themes.diff: Which option lets you talk even about different feelings?
themes.letgo: You do not have to be together always, or smiling always.
themes.want: What kind of time do you need for yourself?

cu10.story: A card about sharing peace of mind and joy with the people close to you.

upright.meaning: Think about who you want to spend time with, and how. A small thank-you or conversation is also a step toward growing a relationship that feels safe.

themes.blind: Are you overlooking small joys with the people close to you?
themes.caution: Do not assume everyone wants the same happiness.
themes.diff: Which option lets you continue at ease with people who matter?
themes.letgo: You do not have to make a big success the condition for happiness.
themes.want: With whom, and what kind of days, do you want to spend your time?

cu10.hint: The Ten of Cups is a scene of a family spreading their arms under a rainbow while children dance. Beyond personal success, it represents harmony and happiness built with the people who matter. In a decision, picture how that choice changes your life with the people close to you. Floating the faces of family, partner, and companions one by one, and thinking about the effect on each, lets your priorities appear naturally. Putting your ideal life into words also helps reduce indecision.
cu10.scene: This card stays close to indecision concerning your whole life — the balance of work and family, choosing where to live. Reversed, review whether you are tired from the gap between ideal and reality. Rather than demanding a perfect picture, asking what your family wants most right now is the shortcut.
cu10.check: How does that choice change your life with the people close to you? Have you pictured the faces of family and companions, one by one? Can you put your ideal life into words? Have you asked what the person most important to you wants most right now?

decision.text: In a situation concerning your whole life with the people close to you, like buying a house, read this card not by personal conditions alone, but by what kind of time the life will let you spend with the people who matter. Reversed, explore a way for everyone to feel at ease, so true feelings are not hidden behind an appearance of closeness.

cu11.background: A fish peeks out of the cup a young person holds, and the young person looks at the fish — meeting an unexpected feeling or idea with surprise.
cu11.name: Page of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you deciding promises based only on the mood of the moment? Give it a little time and check whether you feel the same.

themes.blind: Are you being swept along by the mood of the moment?
themes.caution: If your words and feelings change, tell the other person too.
themes.diff: Which option lets you reconsider even if your feelings change?
themes.letgo: It is fine not to feel the way you expected.
themes.want: What would you still treasure after some time has passed?

cu11.story: A card about noticing small shifts in feeling, and small inspirations.
cu11.symbol: Water / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: Page (sensitivity, news)

upright.meaning: Put what suddenly caught your attention into words or a picture. Even if you cannot explain it well, it can be a chance to know your own feelings.

themes.blind: Are you missing a feeling that suddenly surfaced?
themes.caution: Do not make a big promise on inspiration alone.
themes.diff: Which option lets you test a small feeling or idea?
themes.letgo: Even if you cannot explain it well, writing it down is fine.
themes.want: What moved your heart?

cu11.hint: The Page of Cups meets the eyes of a fish that has peeked out of the cup. It is a card representing an unexpected inspiration, and the small surprise brought by an honest sensitivity. In a decision, do not treat lightly the sensation of 'somehow, I am drawn to this,' which logic cannot explain. Intuition can be born from the accumulation of your experience so far. Noting that sensation down and rereading it after a few days to check whether the same feeling continues lets you tell an impulse from your true heart.
cu11.scene: This card often appears for indecision where sensitivity is tested — creative work, a new hobby, approaching someone you are drawn to. Reversed, watch that the swings of your mood are not shaking your judgment. Thinking it over once more when your feelings are calm, and seeing whether the same answer appears, is a way to check.
cu11.check: Have you left a note of a feeling you are drawn to but cannot explain? After rereading it in a few days, does the same feeling continue? Are the swings of your mood shaking your judgment? Are you allowing yourself a playful heart?

decision.text: In a situation of turning a suddenly-sprung feeling into action, like contacting someone, read this card by using that sensation — even if you cannot explain it well — as a chance to know your own feelings. Reversed, check whether you are deciding even promises on the mood of the moment, and whether you would feel the same after a pause.

cu12.background: A knight on a white horse holds out a cup as if offering it. The horse advances calmly — inviting or proposing while thinking of the other person.
cu12.name: Knight of Cups

reversed.meaning: Are you reassured by lovely words alone? Check whether the actual actions and promises match, and how you yourself feel.

themes.blind: Do the beautiful words and the actual actions match?
themes.caution: Do not decide a promise based on atmosphere alone.
themes.diff: Which option can you trust in actions, not just words?
themes.letgo: You do not have to accept just to avoid disappointing the other person.
themes.want: Do you truly want to accept that invitation?

cu12.story: A card about delivering feelings that matter through words and actions.
cu12.symbol: Water / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: Knight (proposals, romance)

upright.meaning: If you have feelings to share, think of words that do not strain the other person. You can also answer an invitation after checking your own feelings.

themes.blind: Have you put what you want to tell the other person into words?
themes.caution: Even when sharing feelings, respect the other person's answer.
themes.diff: Which option allows a proposal that strains neither of you?
themes.letgo: You do not have to hide everything out of embarrassment.
themes.want: What kind of invitation would make you happy?

cu12.hint: The Knight of Cups rides a white horse, holding a cup in offering and advancing slowly. He is a knight who treasures romance, delivering a sincere proposal without rushing. In a decision, the key is checking not gain and loss, but 'is this a choice honest to my own feelings?' When you receive a proposal or invitation, also look at whether the other person's words match their actions. Letting beautiful words move your heart while confirming a single piece of backing makes your judgment far more certain.
cu12.scene: This card pushes your back when you are torn about accepting a heartfelt proposal, or sharing your own feelings. Reversed, inspect whether you are being swept by surface charm or idealization. Writing down just one realistic condition and comparing it lets you treasure both romance and reality.
cu12.check: Is that choice honest to your own feelings? Do the other person's words and actions match? Have you compared the beautiful ideal against even one real condition? If you were to share your feelings, in what words would you deliver them?

decision.text: In a situation of receiving an invitation or an offer in love, read this card by whether the choice is honest to your own feelings, rather than by gain and loss. Look also at whether the words were delivered slowly and sincerely. Reversed, do not be reassured by lovely words alone — check that they match actual actions and promises.

cu13.background: By the sea, the queen gazes at a lidded cup. What is inside cannot be seen from outside — a reminder that a person's heart cannot be fully known just by looking.
cu13.name: Queen of Cups

reversed.meaning: Do you feel you must somehow fix the other person's mood yourself? While treasuring them, it is fine to take time to rest yourself, too.

themes.blind: Are you putting your own tiredness last?
themes.caution: Do not make the other person's mood your responsibility.
themes.diff: Which option lets you rest yourself while treasuring others?
themes.letgo: You do not have to whittle yourself down to be kind.
themes.want: What do you want someone to do for you right now?

cu13.story: A card about listening to another's feelings while treasuring your own.
cu13.symbol: Water / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: Queen (empathy, intuition)

upright.meaning: Rather than answering right away, try listening to the other person. Trying to understand their feelings can itself lead to peace of mind.

themes.blind: Might listening be needed more than answering?
themes.caution: Do not assume you fully understand the other person's feelings.
themes.diff: Which option lets you listen to each other's feelings calmly?
themes.letgo: You do not have to solve it for them right away.
themes.want: What kind of connection do you want to treasure?

cu13.hint: The Queen of Cups sits on a throne by the sea, gazing at a lidded cup. She is a person who deeply draws out others' feelings while also listening carefully to her own inner voice. In a decision, the power to stay close to the emotions around you is a strength — but check that prioritizing others' feelings has not made you lose sight of your own true heart. In a quiet place, with no one's expectations in the picture, ask 'what do I truly want?' and the answer surfaces.
cu13.scene: This card often appears when you stand in a position of supporting someone and postpone your own choices. Reversed, watch that you are not being swept into the other person's emotions until the boundary blurs. Distinguishing between caring and carrying lets you decide while keeping your kindness.
cu13.check: With no one's expectations in the picture, what do you truly want? Prioritizing others' feelings, are you postponing your own true heart? Can you distinguish between caring and carrying? Do you have a place to think quietly?

decision.text: In a situation where the other person's feelings sway, like caregiving, read this card as first taking the time to listen and try to understand their feelings, rather than producing an answer right away. Reversed, protect your own time to rest, so you do not carry too much in trying to fix the other person's mood.

cu14.background: The king sits holding a cup above a wavy sea. Though the surroundings sway, the king's figure is calm — the power to choose your actions while feeling your emotions.
cu14.name: King of Cups
cu14.story: A card about facing people calmly even when your feelings sway.
cu14.symbol: Water / Cups (feelings, relationships) / Court card: King (maturity, embrace)

upright.meaning: Even with anger or anxiety, you do not have to reply right away. After settling a little, choose words that are good for both you and the other person.

themes.blind: Are you making time to settle yourself?
themes.caution: Separate feeling an emotion from acting on it as-is.
themes.diff: Which option lets you face things with consideration and calm?
themes.letgo: You do not have to think having emotions makes you weak.
themes.want: How would you like to speak, both to yourself and to the other person?

reversed.meaning: Are you hiding your feelings for too long, or using them to move others? Try sharing your own feelings in words that do not blame.

themes.blind: Are you hiding your true feelings behind a pretense of being fine?
themes.caution: Do not try to move the other person with a bad mood.
themes.want: What do you truly want to say?
themes.letgo: You do not have to swallow everything — putting it into words is fine.
themes.diff: Which option lets you share feelings without blame?

cu14.hint: The King of Cups holds a cup calmly on a throne floating on a rough sea. It is a card representing a maturity that does not deny the waves of emotion, and judges without wavering on top of them. In a decision, it teaches that even while feeling anxiety or impatience, you can hold them and still choose calmly. Rather than trying to erase the emotion, acknowledge 'I am feeling anxious right now,' then line up your material for judgment again. The capacity to receive the feelings of the people around you also comes alive in this choice.
cu14.scene: This is a reassuring card in situations with an emotional person or circumstance, where an adult judgment is asked of you. Reversed, review whether bottling up your true heart is turning your decision cold. Sharing your emotions in words is also part of a mature choice.
cu14.check: Can you name and acknowledge the emotion you are feeling right now? Even while holding the emotion, can you line up your material for judgment calmly? Do you have the room to receive the feelings of those around you? Are you bottling up your true heart too much?

decision.text: In a situation where emotions run high, like apologizing, read this card as not replying in the grip of anger or anxiety, but settling a little first and choosing words that are good for both you and the other person. Reversed, explore a way to share without bottling your feelings up forever, in words that do not blame.

sw01.background: A hand from a cloud raises a straight sword high, with a crown at its tip. It shows sorting out a confusing matter and finding what matters.
sw01.name: Ace of Swords

reversed.meaning: Are you trying to reach an answer inside your head alone? Check the information, and arrange your words before you speak to the other person.

themes.blind: Can you separate what you know from what you are guessing?
themes.caution: Do not state a conclusion before checking.
themes.diff: Which option lets you confirm information and think again?
themes.letgo: You do not have to produce the right answer right now.
themes.want: If you thought calmly, what would you want to say?

sw01.story: A card about organizing your thoughts and making what matters clear.

upright.meaning: Write down the facts you know and find the single most important point. If you can explain your reason briefly, choosing for yourself becomes easier.

themes.blind: Is there information you have not organized yet?
themes.caution: Even if you believe you are right, do not turn it into harsh words.
themes.diff: Which option lets you organize the facts and explain your reason?
themes.letgo: You do not have to take on everything while it stays vague.
themes.want: What do you most want to make clear?

sw01.hint: The Ace of Swords is a scene of a hand extending from the clouds, holding high a sword crowned with a wreath. It represents the clarity that cuts through a tangled situation in one stroke. In a decision, begin by putting the cause of your indecision into words. When you can write 'what I am torn about' in a single sentence, half the answer is already there. Separate fact from assumption, and clarify what information the decision needs. But a sharp sword can wound people too — choose the words that deliver your conclusion with care.
sw01.scene: When you want to reach a conclusion on a problem you have worried over for a long time, this card says you may be able to see it clearly now. Reversed, check whether too much information is confusing you, or whether you are trying to push through with strong words. Simply writing your thoughts out on paper can clear the fog.
sw01.check: Can you write what you are torn about in a single sentence? Have you sorted fact from assumption? What information is still missing for the decision? Will the words you use to deliver the conclusion hurt anyone unnecessarily? Might you be able to see it clearly right now?

decision.text: In a situation where conditions are tangled and judgment dulls, like cancelling a contract, read this card by writing down the facts you know and narrowing to the single point that matters most. Whether you can explain your reasons briefly is the yardstick. Reversed, do not try to answer it all inside your head — verify where your information comes from, and settle your words.

sw02.background: A person with covered eyes crosses two swords before their chest, with the sea behind. They keep their balance, while there is something they are choosing not to look at.
sw02.name: Two of Swords

reversed.meaning: Have you gathered so much information that deciding became harder? Narrow it to the conditions you need, and check the things you were avoiding, too.

themes.blind: With too much information, are you more lost instead?
themes.caution: Before deciding in a rush, narrow down the conditions that matter.
themes.diff: Which option makes it easier to narrow down by your own conditions?
themes.letgo: It is fine to reduce information you gathered for thinking.
themes.want: Is the reason for your hesitation a feeling, or a lack of information?

sw02.story: A card about the feeling of being torn between two and not yet able to decide.
sw02.symbol: Air / Swords (thought, judgment) / Number 2 (balance, holding off)

upright.meaning: If you cannot decide now, think about what you would need to know to choose. Lining up both sides' information, including the points you would rather not see, can help.

themes.blind: Is there something you are avoiding because you do not want to see it?
themes.caution: If you wait, think about what you will check before deciding.
themes.diff: Which option lets you gather the information you need and compare?
themes.letgo: You do not have to keep searching for an answer that satisfies everyone.
themes.want: If you owed no one any consideration, which way would you go?

sw02.hint: The woman in the Two of Swords is blindfolded, two swords crossed before her chest. She is a figure protecting her peace of mind by choosing neither and keeping the balance. In a decision, it matters to notice that holding off has itself become a choice. Removing the blindfold — verifying the information you have been avoiding — often lets the scale tip on its own. Try to tell whether your reason for being unable to decide is a lack of information, or fear of being hurt.
sw02.scene: When time passes with neither of two options chosen, this card reflects that deadlock. Reversed, it is either finally the time to step into a decision, or confusion from too much information. Set a deadline, narrow what you will verify by then to just one thing, and you can start to move.
sw02.check: Has not deciding itself become a choice? What information are you avoiding? Is your reason for being unable to decide a lack of information, or fear of being hurt? Can you narrow what you will verify before the deadline to one thing?

decision.text: In a situation balanced with no decisive edge either way, like going or not going, read this card by accepting that holding off is itself a choice, and thinking about what you would need to know in order to choose. Reversed, check whether gathering too much information is making it harder to decide, and narrow down the conditions you truly need.

sw03.background: Under rain clouds, three swords overlap a heart — an image that draws sadness plainly. It is not a prediction that you will be hurt, but a hint to receive the pain you already feel with care.
sw03.name: Three of Swords

reversed.meaning: Separate the parts that have eased a little from the parts that still hurt. Without forcing yourself to recover quickly, you can also ask someone you can talk to, to listen.

themes.blind: Which parts have eased a little, and which still hurt?
themes.caution: Do not rush yourself to feel better quickly.
themes.diff: Which option lets you sort your feelings without strain?
themes.letgo: You do not have to forgive, or forget, right away.
themes.want: Is there someone you can safely talk to about your feelings?

sw03.story: A card about not pretending a hurt feeling never happened.

upright.meaning: You do not have to hide that something hurt behind a pretense of being fine. Put what was hard into words, and make time to rest.

themes.blind: Can you acknowledge that you were hurt?
themes.caution: When things are hard, you do not have to rush to decide an answer.
themes.diff: Which option lets you treat your own feelings with care?
themes.letgo: You do not have to keep pretending to be fine.
themes.want: How would you like to be treated right now?

sw03.hint: The Three of Swords draws, without hiding it, a heart pierced by swords under rain clouds. It is a card showing that admitting pain is the entrance to healing. In a decision, take care not to decide big things immediately after being hurt. Inside pain, what you lost looms large and your options narrow. First put into words what hurt you, and have someone you trust listen. The decision can wait until the rain eases a little.
sw03.scene: This card often appears after heartbreak, betrayal, or a disappointing result, when you are torn about what to do. Reversed, the pain is beginning to ease — but check that an old wound is not shadowing your judgment. Thinking about this choice separately from past pain lets you face it calmly.
sw03.check: In the middle of pain, are you rushing a big decision? Can you put into words what hurt you? Have you had someone you trust listen to you? Can you think about this choice separately from the pain of the past?

decision.text: In a situation where heartbreak lingers, like getting back together, read this card by not hiding the pain but admitting it first, and putting big decisions off until after. Put what was hard into words, and take time to rest. Reversed, separate what has eased from what still hurts, and let having someone listen be part of your material.

sw04.background: Inside a quiet building, the figure of a knight lies with hands joined. Swords rest nearby — time away from conflict and busyness, to rest.
sw04.name: Four of Swords

reversed.meaning: Check your own state: is your rest insufficient, or are you ready to start moving? If you start, beginning with fewer plans is fine.

themes.blind: Have you checked whether you truly rested?
themes.caution: If you start moving, begin with fewer plans.
themes.diff: Which option lets you restart at a pace that fits your state?
themes.letgo: You do not have to immediately handle the same amount as before your rest.
themes.want: Right now, do you want to rest, or to move a little?

sw04.story: A card about pausing the constant motion and settling your heart and mind.

upright.meaning: Before rushing an answer, rest a little. Taking time away from your worries can change how things look afterward.

themes.blind: Are you tired from thinking too much?
themes.caution: Do not fill even your rest time with plans.
themes.diff: Which option gives you time to rest your mind and heart?
themes.letgo: You do not have to think of resting as slacking.
themes.want: What would you like to step away from, to rest?

sw04.hint: The Four of Swords is the statue of a knight lying in the quiet of a church. It represents not someone who quit the fight, but someone resting in preparation for what is next. In a decision, it teaches that sometimes 'not deciding now' is the best judgment. Judgment made in a state of exhaustion inevitably narrows your field of view. If the deadline allows, step away from the problem for a few days and put sleep and meals in order. Looking at the same problem after resting, the answer often looks surprisingly simple.
sw04.scene: This card often appears when decision after decision is demanded amid busyness and your head will not turn. Reversed, it is either restless impatience at being unable to rest, or the timing to restart. Tell whether your body wants to move or your impatience is hurrying you, then move.
sw04.check: Are you trying to judge with an exhausted mind? Is there room to extend the deadline and rest? Are you getting enough sleep and food? If you looked at the same problem after resting, how would you see it? Can you set the timing of your restart yourself?

decision.text: In a situation of rushing an answer with a tired mind, like whether to take time off work, read this card as the judgment 'not deciding now' itself sometimes being the best one. Taking time away from the worrying can change how things look later. Reversed, check from your own condition whether you are short on rest, or ready to move.

sw05.background: Behind a person holding swords, two people walk away. Swords also lie on the ground. Even when someone wins, it is a scene where not everyone is glad.
sw05.name: Five of Swords

reversed.meaning: Look for a way other than continuing the fight. Talking it out, apologizing, or taking distance are also choices that protect you.

themes.blind: Is there a way to end the conflict you have not tried yet?
themes.caution: Even after apologizing, do not keep enduring beyond reason.
themes.diff: Which option lets you choose how it ends, calmly?
themes.letgo: You do not have to treat withdrawing as always losing.
themes.want: Do you want to talk it out, or take some distance?

sw05.story: A card about asking what you lose when you cling to winning.

upright.meaning: Has defeating the other person in words become the real goal? Consider whether the relationships and peace of mind that matter will still remain after you win.

themes.blind: What might you lose in order to win?
themes.caution: Do not use cruel words to win an argument.
themes.diff: Which option protects the relationships and peace of mind that matter?
themes.letgo: You do not have to join every fight.
themes.want: After winning, what do you want to still have left?

sw05.hint: In the Five of Swords, the victor gathers up swords while the two defeated turn their backs and leave. It depicts a barren victory — you supposedly won, yet lost something. In a decision, question whether winning the argument or negotiation is truly your purpose. Is what you gain by defeating someone in words worth the loss of the relationship? If your purpose lies elsewhere, choosing to withdraw without clinging to victory is also wise. Deciding in advance how far you can concede helps you avoid a war of attrition.
sw05.scene: When you are torn about pushing your claim through inside a conflict, this card urges you to estimate the cost. Reversed, the time to accept reconciliation or defeat has come, though a bad aftertaste may remain. A single small word — apologizing, admitting — can be the chance to rebuild the relationship.
sw05.check: Is winning this argument your true purpose? Is what you gain by winning worth the relationship you lose? Have you decided in advance how far you can concede? Might a single word — apologizing, admitting — change the situation?

decision.text: In a situation where winning the argument easily becomes the purpose, like lending and borrowing money, read this card by whether an important relationship and peace of mind remain after you win. Reversed, put methods other than continuing the fight — talking it out, apologizing, keeping distance — into your options too.

sw06.background: An adult and a child ride in a boat, carried by a boatman. Six swords stand in the boat. Even with worries remaining, it is the figure of moving toward calmer ground.
sw06.name: Six of Swords

reversed.meaning: Is the reason you cannot move preparation, or feeling? Separate them one by one, and look for the parts where someone can help.

themes.blind: Concretely, what is the reason you cannot move?
themes.caution: Separate your worries one by one, and look for what others can help with.
themes.diff: Which option lets you advance the preparation little by little?
themes.letgo: You can rely on others without first settling everything about the past.
themes.want: What peace of mind do you want on the other side of the change?

sw06.story: A card about moving away, little by little, from a difficult place.

upright.meaning: Look for a place or a method where you can feel safer than now. Even before everything is solved, you can have someone help you.

themes.blind: Have you been able to look for a place safer than where you are?
themes.caution: If you change places, think about the preparation and support you need.
themes.diff: Which option lets you borrow help and move toward calmer ground?
themes.letgo: You do not have to keep striving in a difficult place.
themes.want: What kind of days might feel a little easier?

sw06.hint: In the Six of Swords, a ferryman quietly rows a boat, carrying people from rough water toward a calm shore. It represents a transition period of escaping difficulty and gradually improving circumstances. In a decision, it teaches that rather than solving the problem all at once, there is meaning in first leaving your current place. The swords still standing in the boat also mean you can advance without discarding all your past indecision. Borrowing the help of someone you trust matters too.
sw06.scene: When you are torn about changing your environment, this card supports a calm departure. Reversed, your departure may be delayed, or you may be dragging the past along. Rather than waiting for perfect preparation, consider moving with just the minimum needed to board the boat.
sw06.check: By leaving your current place, what becomes easier? Can you start moving without waiting for perfect preparation? Even carrying past indecision with you, is there a way forward? Is there a trusted person who will row the boat for you?

decision.text: In a situation of relocating and starting over, like a job transfer, read this card by not trying to solve everything at once, but moving toward the calmer side while borrowing someone's help too. Reversed, separate whether what stops you is preparation or feelings, and search for the parts where you can be helped.

sw07.background: A person carries five swords away from a row of tents. Two swords remain behind. It holds both the resourcefulness of advancing by another route than head-on, and the risk of moving in secret.
sw07.name: Seven of Swords
sw07.story: A card about ingenuity in method, and about the problem of keeping secrets.

upright.meaning: If the usual method is difficult, think of another way. But you need to check that it does not involve lying or breaking an important promise.

themes.blind: Could you use a method different from the usual one?
themes.caution: Separate being resourceful from telling lies.
themes.diff: Which option lets you be resourceful while keeping your promises?
themes.letgo: You do not have to choose only the head-on method.
themes.want: Why do you want to advance alone?

reversed.meaning: Is there something you are hiding, or something important you have not shared? Think about the range you can speak of, and look for a way to protect trust.

themes.blind: Is there something important you have not shared?
themes.caution: Before piling on more cover-ups, think about how to talk about it.
themes.want: What would feel a little lighter if you shared it honestly?
themes.letgo: You do not have to keep hiding a failure forever.
themes.diff: Which option lets you advance without adding more secrets?

sw07.hint: The man in the Seven of Swords is about to slip away from camp carrying swords. It is an ambiguous card, readable as ingenuity and quick thinking, or as sneaking and deceiving. In a decision, discern whether choosing a detour instead of going head-on is truly a wise strategy, or simply avoiding facing it. Whether you could stand behind the method even if it came out later is the yardstick that separates good ingenuity from a guilty means.
sw07.scene: This card often appears when you are torn between proceeding silently and confiding in the people involved. Reversed, what you hid may come to light, or the time to speak honestly has come. Telling them yourself first tends to damage trust less than them finding out.
sw07.check: Is that way of doing it something you could stand behind even if it came out later? Is the detour a wise strategy, or an escape from facing it? Is there someone it would be better to tell first, rather than proceeding silently? Are you carrying too much alone?

decision.text: In a situation with circumstances hard to say head-on, like whether to tell your company about a side job, read this card by the need for detour-like ingenuity alongside checking that it does not become a lie or a broken promise. Reversed, check whether there is something important you are hiding, and search for a way to protect trust by deciding the range you can talk about.

sw08.background: A person with covered eyes is surrounded by eight swords. Between the swords, there are gaps, too. When you feel unable to move, it is an image suggesting there may be a path you have not noticed yet.
sw08.name: Eight of Swords

reversed.meaning: Check one reason you believed you could not do it. A small change of method, or someone's help, may reveal a part that can move.

themes.blind: Have your available methods grown compared to before?
themes.caution: Do not change everything at once — choose a small step.
themes.diff: Which option widens what you can do, little by little?
themes.letgo: It is fine to try again something you could not do before.
themes.want: What kind of help would let you move?

sw08.story: A card about re-examining your reasons for thinking you cannot.

upright.meaning: You do not have to blame the difficulty on yourself alone. Separate what truly cannot be done from what you have not tried yet, and think about how to borrow help.

themes.blind: What truly cannot be done, and what have you not tried yet?
themes.caution: Do not blame the difficulty entirely on yourself.
themes.diff: Which option lets you use help or another method?
themes.letgo: You do not have to decide that something is impossible for you.
themes.want: If one restriction disappeared, what would you want to do?

sw08.hint: The woman in the Eight of Swords is blindfolded and surrounded by swords, but the ropes are loose and the swords only stand lined up like a fence. It represents a state where an exit exists, yet you believe you cannot move. In a decision, try writing down, one by one, your reasons for feeling 'it is hopeless anyway.' Among them there will be assumptions you have never verified. Simply explaining the situation to someone can have them point out an escape route you could not see yourself.
sw08.scene: This card often appears when you feel blocked on all sides and unable to move. Reversed, you are removing the blindfold yourself and your power to escape is returning. Trying a small first step — one email, one phone call — can move the situation faster than you expected.
sw08.check: Can you write down, one by one, your reasons for feeling 'it is hopeless anyway'? Among them, is there an assumption you have never verified? If you explained the situation to someone, might they point out an escape route? What is the first small step?

decision.text: In a situation where you cannot take a step forward in love, read this card by separating what truly cannot be done from what you simply have not tried yet. The ropes are loose and there is an exit, yet you may be convinced you cannot move. Reversed, verify just one of the reasons you thought you could not, and start from a small change.

sw09.background: On a bed, a person covers their face with both hands. Nine swords line the wall. It shows the weight of a heart whose worries swell at night.
sw09.name: Nine of Swords

reversed.meaning: Put your feelings into words and share them with someone. Even if nothing is solved right away, you can start by finding a way not to carry it alone.

themes.blind: Is there a worry you can now put into words?
themes.caution: Even if things ease a little, do not take on everything by force.
themes.diff: Which option lets you share your feelings with the people around you?
themes.letgo: You do not have to hide hard feelings — relying on others is fine.
themes.want: Who would you like to listen, and to what?

sw09.story: A card about worry and self-blame growing large.

upright.meaning: Write down, separately, what you are worried about and what actually happened. Rather than thinking alone forever, having someone listen matters too.

themes.blind: Can you separate worry from what actually happened?
